saying: they may see for themselves that they are but beasts
source: Drawn from the BSB, STEPBible TAHOT and TAGNT, and the commentaries named under each note.

layers.evidence: Rests on the verse's statement that God tests people to show them their state.
layers.text: Solomon reflects that God lets wrongs go on for a time in order to test people, so that they will see that, as mortal creatures, they are frail and die just like the animals.

layers.evidence: Keil-Delitzsch say hemmah takes up behemah as an echo, a play on words that accompanies the thought. Bullinger notes the repeated they is a figure adding emphasis.

cites.at: E. W. Bullinger, Figures of Speech Used in the Bible (1898)

layers.text: The Hebrew behind they are but beasts runs shehem behemah hemmah. The word for they (hem, hemmah) echoes the sound of the word for beasts (behemah), and the doubled they adds emphasis, so the line drives home how close mortal people stand to the animals.
